root_idea.summary: The root centers on forceful removal and exclusion, especially banishment under condemnation.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of driving away develops into cursing: for God, exclusion from mercy, guidance, and ultimately blessedness; for people, an invocation of condemnation against another. Reciprocal and reflexive cursing constructions develop from the same semantic field.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested feminine noun denoting a curse.
Quran-attested active participle, normalized to its singular citation form.
Feminine passive participle normalized under the singular masculine citation form.
Masculine plural passive participle normalized under the singular citation form.

senses.definition: To curse: to invoke or impose banishment from mercy as an expression of condemnation.
senses.usage_conditions: When attributed to God, the curse denotes exclusion from mercy and guidance in this world and punishment or banishment in the Hereafter. When attributed to people, it is a supplication or invocation against another. Active and passive voice express the same lexical action and result.

senses.definition: Cursing; the act or invocation of pronouncing a curse.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun for the act of invoking condemnation or exclusion from mercy; the Quranic occurrence appears in an intensified construction.

senses.definition: A curse; an imposed state or sentence of exclusion from mercy.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a countable or definite noun, including in expressions such as God's curse and the curse upon a people or party.

senses.definition: One who curses; one who invokes a curse against another.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural refers to those who pronounce curses, in a construction where they curse people who conceal or suppress revealed guidance.

senses.definition: Accursed; subjected to condemnation and exclusion from mercy.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally or substantively for one placed under a curse; the Quranic forms include feminine singular and masculine plural inflections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is much cursed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal epithet, distinct in vocalization and meaning from the Quranic noun لَعْنَة meaning “a curse.”
A personal epithet describing habitual cursing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An expelled or banished person; also a wolf, as a conventional Classical Arabic designation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical usage of the adjective, separate from the Quranic active participle لَاعِن and from the passive sense “accursed.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The base or lower part of a palm-tree raceme.
Mutual cursing, in which each party curses himself or the other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The three labels are explicitly associated with the reciprocal cursing construction; no narrower legal or procedural sense is assumed here.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Personal epithet for a man who is much cursed.
Specialized botanical meaning: the base of a palm raceme.

cautions: The Quran-only plural active participle لَاعِنُون and the feminine and masculine plural passive participles مَلْعُونَة and مَلْعُونِين are normalized to singular dictionary citation forms.
The Quranic noun لَعْنَة meaning “a curse” is distinct in vocalization and meaning from the Classical personal epithet لُعْنَة meaning “a person who is much cursed.”
